title: Terms of service — Niko
doc.title: Terms of service
doc.intro: By using Niko in a Discord server, you agree to these terms, Discord’s Terms of Service, and Discord’s Community Guidelines. They apply to the official public Niko instances described below.
s0.title: 1. Acceptance
s0.body: By inviting Niko to a server, using its commands, or using the website and dashboard, you agree to these terms. If you do not agree, remove the bot and stop using the site. If you accept on behalf of a server, you confirm you are allowed to do so.
s1.title: 2. Scope: official instances and self-hosted instances
s1.body:
These terms cover the official public Niko instances we operate: the bot invited from niko.sryze.cc and everything served from that domain.
- **Official public instances** store all user data in a private MongoDB database we control, as described in the Privacy Policy.
- **Private, beta, and self-hosted instances** are copies run by other people. They may use the deprecated SQLite storage method, a different database, or plain files, and their data may be held anywhere.
- **We do not control self-hosted instances.** We do not operate, host, or administer them and cannot see or change their data. We therefore cannot provide support, moderation, safety, access, or data-removal help for them, and we are not responsible for their uptime, security, content, or legal compliance. Requests about those instances must go to their operator.
- If you run your own instance, you are its operator and its controller: you are responsible for its security, for answering requests from its users, for what it stores and for how long, and for complying with Discord's rules and the law where you and its users are.
s2.title: 3. Eligibility
s2.body: You must be old enough to use Discord where you live (at least 13, or older where local law requires) and old enough to enter a contract to buy premium, or have permission from a parent or guardian. If you are under the age of majority where you live, you confirm a parent or guardian has reviewed these terms with you.
s3.title: 4. Permitted use
s3.body: Use Niko for personal, non-commercial community features. Do not use it to harass, spam, harm, violate law, exploit, reverse-engineer, resell as a service, or disrupt the service or other servers. Do not attempt to access data, commands, or staff areas you are not authorised to use, and do not use Niko to evade a blacklist, mute, or investigation.
s4.title: 5. Availability and changes
s4.body: Niko is provided as-is, on a best-effort basis, without an uptime, latency, or feature-retention guarantee. Features may change, be restricted, or be removed without notice, and data may be lost in a failure. Niko is not a paid-critical or life-safety service, and you should not rely on it as one. Keep your own copies of anything you need to keep.
s5.title: 6. Moderation and blacklists
s5.body: The operator may blacklist a user or server for abuse, exploitation, or a violation of these terms or the Community Policy, with or without notice, and may restrict features per server. A blacklist can be appealed once through the appeals process; an appeal does not guarantee reinstatement, and using a data-removal request to escape a restriction is itself a violation.
s6.title: 7. AI-generated content and Groq
s6.body:
Niko's AI replies, image understanding, and voice transcription are provided through [Groq](https://groq.com). When the AI feature is enabled on a server, the message being answered and the limited context described in the Privacy Policy are sent to Groq to generate a reply, and Groq's own terms and privacy policy apply to that request.
AI output can be inaccurate, incomplete, biased, or unexpected. Automated moderation — including premium image scoring — is a helper, not a substitute for human moderation. Verify important information independently. The operator is not liable for harm from generated content or from a missed or mistaken classification. Operators of self-hosted instances may point their copy at a different provider; their choice is theirs, not ours.
s7.title: 8. Payments and crypto
s7.body: Payments are collected through OxaPay, a third-party payment processor. Crypto transactions are irreversible once broadcast to the network, and the amount of crypto you send is set by the network and the provider's quote. You are responsible for sending the correct asset on the correct network, and for any taxes that apply to you. OxaPay's terms also apply to the payment itself. Never send funds to an address copied from somewhere other than the checkout page Niko shows you. If you believe a charge is wrong, contact support first; please do not start a chargeback or payment dispute for a service that was actually delivered, except where the law gives you that right.
s8.title: 9. Refunds
s8.body: Premium and donations are purchases of digital services delivered immediately and are generally non-refundable. If a payment was duplicated, charged in error, or never activated, contact us through the support server and we will review it in good faith and, where appropriate, extend the term, issue a credit, or arrange a refund through the processor. Nothing in these terms limits a mandatory consumer right you have under the law that applies to you.
s9.title: 10. Premium subscriptions
s9.body: Niko Premium costs $15 USD per server per month and is billed manually: you choose to renew, and a reminder is sent before the term ends. There is no automatic recurring charge. Premium is a licence to use server features for one server and one term; it is not a sale of software, does not create a partnership or fiduciary relationship, and does not give you any ownership in Niko. Premium follows the server, not the person who paid, and it is not transferable to another server without our agreement.
s10.title: 11. Economy and virtual items
s10.body: In-bot currency and items have no real-world value and cannot be exchanged for money or goods. Balances may be reset, corrected, or wiped — for example after an exploit, a duplication bug, or a season reset. Premium is separate from virtual items and is never granted for in-bot currency. Buying, selling, or trading in-bot value for real money is not permitted.
s11.title: 12. Data retention and deletion
s11.body:
The Privacy Policy sets out exactly what official instances keep, for how long, and what survives a deletion request. In summary: personal and configuration data is kept until you remove it or complete a [data removal request](/data-removal); AI conversation memory is a rolling window you can erase with `/clearhistory`; anonymous counters are kept for 90 days plus lifetime totals; and moderation and safety records — blacklists, warnings, mutes, moderation cases, logs and ticket transcripts, giveaway bans, abuse strikes, and scam-image reports — are retained to protect communities and cannot be erased through that form.
Using a deletion request to bypass a ban, warning, giveaway restriction, or investigation is a violation of these terms, and requests are reviewed before deletion runs. Where the law requires release of a retained record, a formal legal request with a court record or signed legal document and an official legal contact must be emailed to the bot owner at [owner@niko.sryze.cc](mailto:owner@niko.sryze.cc); those matters are handled personally and confidentially. Self-hosted instances set their own retention and handle their own requests; we cannot delete or release data we do not hold.
s12.title: 13. Volunteer-run project
s12.body: Niko is a free, volunteer-run community project. It is not a company, partnership, registered business, or other legal entity. The project is maintained by individuals in their personal capacity, in their own time, without payment from subscription revenue beyond covering service costs. No volunteer, contributor, or maintainer is your employee, agent, partner, or fiduciary, and none of them makes any personal promise about the service.
s13.title: 14. Third-party services
s13.body: Niko depends on services we do not control, including Discord, Groq, OxaPay, fal.ai, and hosting providers. Outages, policy changes, price changes, or account actions on those services can interrupt or end features. We are not responsible for third-party services, and we are not affiliated with or endorsed by Discord, Groq, OxaPay, or fal.ai.
s14.title: 15. Limitation of liability
s14.body: To the maximum extent permitted by law, the operator, maintainers, and volunteers are not liable for indirect, incidental, special, consequential, exemplary, or punitive damages, or for lost profits, revenue, data, goodwill, or server growth, arising from or related to Niko, premium, or any payment. Our total aggregate liability for all claims relating to a server's subscription is limited to the greater of the amount actually paid for that subscription in the three months before the claim or $15 USD. This does not limit liability that cannot be limited by law.
s15.title: 16. Indemnity
s15.body: To the maximum extent permitted by law, you agree to indemnify and hold harmless the operator, maintainers, and volunteers from claims, damages, losses, and reasonable costs arising from your server's use of Niko, content posted in it, your breach of these terms, or your violation of another person's rights.
s16.title: 17. Changes and discontinuation
s16.body: We may change, suspend, or discontinue Niko or premium, including a specific feature. If premium is discontinued during a paid term, we will handle the remaining term in good faith, for example by keeping the service running to the end of the term or by offering a pro-rata credit through the processor. We do not guarantee a cash refund where the law does not require one. If any provision of these terms is unenforceable, the rest stays in effect, and these terms are governed by the law that applies to the operator's place of residence, without overriding mandatory protections you have where you live.
s17.title: 18. Contact
s17.body: Questions, payment issues, and data requests can be sent through the Niko [support server](/discord). Data removal has its own page at [/data-removal](/data-removal), and formal legal requests go to the owner at [owner@niko.sryze.cc](mailto:owner@niko.sryze.cc). Include the server ID and the payment or order reference so we can help quickly. Requests about a self-hosted instance must go to that instance's operator.
